missing_arguments.argument: The code gives the two commissioners a broad, continuous role, and this is the strongest code-text support for card 2. They 'participate directly and continuously' in 'review of departmental requests, revenue and expenditure assumptions, specific budgetary requests from other elected officials, and capital planning,' and in 'preparing the recommended budget' (P-013). The commission 'shall submit' the proposal (P-005, P-006), and the recommended budget is 'developed by the budget commission' (P-015). Lines 63 and 147 shorten this to 'reviewing departments' requests.' The clauses on 'revenue and expenditure assumptions' and 'other elected officials' bear directly on two things: the 5% limit, which Resolution 26-0729 says the commission imposed (P-029), and the justice officials' objection to presenting to the panel (P-076).

Full request lists let the full Board adjust the draft, and in the 2026 cycle it did so for most of the protesting offices. Resolution 26-0729 says listing requests 'has allowed the Board of Commissioners to get a true picture of the departments' needs and to make adjustments' (P-028). Card 3 leaves this reason out; it appears only under Option C (line 113). The budget book shows the Board raised four of the six protesting offices above the proposal: sheriff $156,275,873 to $156,663,989, public defender $28,013,709 to $28,395,566, solicitor-general $14,605,358 to $16,149,063, and court clerk $24,249,511 to $24,620,261. It also raised consent decree funding by $18,157,000 (P-054). That was a year when all extra requests were printed in an appendix (P-049). Caveat for the page: the budget book does not say these changes came from the appendix.

The page omits what disclosure looked like before the limit, as shown in a county record the critics did not write. The 2026 budget message reported 'many unmet requests.' Beyond the requests already considered, it counted 'almost $158 million' in personnel and operating requests and 'over $64 million' in capital requests, sorted 'into tranches for funding consideration' (P-049, P-051). This is in Layer 2 (line 86) but not in card 3's 'What supports it.' There, it would show how large the requests are that a 5% limit could keep out of the draft.

The sheriff's own 2027 deck ties staffing needs to the jail agreement. It lists 'Salary Attrition of $1,628,224 Restore 100% funding for all sworn and professional vacancies and discontinue attrition-based reductions' and 'Increase overtime funding allocation to align with operational realities and Consent Decree mandates' (P-060), and 'Consent Decree Compliance' is among its top-ranked requests (P-061). Card 6 cites the probate court, public defender and solicitor-general, but not the sheriff, the largest justice office ($156,663,989 in 2026, P-054). So it misses the link between the officials' staffing claim and the county-recorded reform of 'improving staffing and supervision' (P-048). The deck also qualifies card 3's line that the base budget covers staff. Label it Uncertain (own account).

unfair_wording.text: A Budget Commission that includes two commissioners is helping draft it, and the full Board decides.
unfair_wording.why: 'Helping' follows the sponsors' 'assist' framing (P-007). It makes the commissioners' role sound secondary, and that role is the very point in dispute. Under the amended code, the commission is the body that 'shall submit' the proposed budget (P-005, P-006), and the recommended budget is 'developed by the budget commission' (P-015). Ellis himself called it 'solely responsible for drafting recommendations' (P-079). The code uses both framings, so the page should state both, for example: 'drafts and submits the proposed budget; the full Board decides.' Line 50 ('helps draft the budget') and line 147 ('help prepare') have the same problem. The sentence also closely echoes card 1's title, which is the supporters' case.

unfair_wording.text: Critics also object to a 5% limit on departments' requests for extra money.
unfair_wording.why: The summary gives the supporters' reason for the commission but gives no reason for this objection. A short clause would add the critics' core point: the limit keeps full requests out of a draft the code says must include all of them (P-005, P-029). The summary should also say that no source gives a reason for the limit (line 121).

unfair_wording.text: In Atlanta News First's report, Commissioner Barrett criticized how the commission was set up, and Commissioner Ellis responded. [P-072, P-073] FOX 5 reported that Ellis addressed the officials' concerns.
unfair_wording.why: This softens Barrett's allegation into a complaint about how the commission was set up; ANF says she 'alleged some current board members are trying to take control of the budget process' (P-072). Meanwhile 'addressed', which is FOX 5's verb, can be read as 'resolved'. Suggested wording: 'Barrett said two colleagues were trying to take control of the budget process' and 'Ellis responded to the officials' concerns.'

unfair_wording.text: 2. Only the full Board can adopt or change the budget.
unfair_wording.why: This is listed under 'What's different this year', but the full Board also adopted the budget before 2026; the county manager only proposed it (P-003). The line repeats the sponsors' reassurance ('preserving the full Board's exclusive authority', P-004) as if it were a new safeguard. Mark it 'Unchanged:' or move it below the list.

unfair_wording.text: Resolution 26-0729 says it would "clarify" the code by adding a ban: "No limits or caps shall be placed" on what any department, agency, elected official or authority can request.
unfair_wording.why: Quoting the single word 'clarify' next to 'by adding a ban' reads as a scare quote. It implies the resolution changes the code rather than clarifying it, which undercuts the critics' claim that the limit already conflicts with the code. The resolution's words are 'to clarify that all departmental budget requests are included in the proposed budget' (P-083). Quote the whole phrase.

unfair_wording.text: Resolution 26-0729 says the 5% cap makes the code's rule on requests "effectively" impossible to meet.
unfair_wording.why: Quoting only the hedge word puts it in the spotlight like a scare quote, when the key word is 'impossible'. Quote the clause instead: the Budget Commission 'is effectively making its mandate to submit a proposed budget that includes the budget requests of the County's departments impossible' (P-029).

unfair_wording.text: It cites advice from The Pew Charitable Trusts to "resist the temptation" of across-the-board cuts.
unfair_wording.why: This drops the most pointed part of the advice the resolution cites: 'resist the temptation to make indiscriminate, across-the-board budget cuts' and 'instead use data and evidence to make strategic decisions' (P-028). Quote it in full.

unfair_wording.text: Requests above 5% can still be seen: the public defender's full request is in its posted slides.
unfair_wording.why: This generalizes from one office, since the other posted decks list requests without amounts (P-061, P-063, P-066). Also, posted slides are not the draft, and the draft is what card 3's claim and the code's 'shall include' rule are about (P-005). Suggested wording: 'Outside the draft, at least one office's full request is public: the public defender's posted slides list $4.7 million.'

unfair_wording.text: The base budget is the money needed to keep up past spending, including staff. [P-086] The resolution says departments may describe broader needs, but only "in narrative form."
unfair_wording.why: The first sentence applies the 2026 definition to the 2027 limit in the present tense. The sheriff's 2027 deck says attrition-based reductions left vacancies unfunded ($1,628,224, P-060), so add 'in the 2026 cycle' and note that. The second sentence turns the critics' complaint into a rebuttal; P-029 offers 'only allows departments to describe broader needs in narrative form' as a grievance. If it stays, note that no source says whether those narratives will appear in the draft.

unfair_wording.text: The resolution does not say the meetings were closed.
unfair_wording.why: This line sits in the critics' 'Who disagrees' slot but argues against them. Either state the disagreement neutrally, for example 'The dispute is over what the draft shows and who hears requests, not whether meetings are open', or move the line to 'What challenges it'.

unfair_wording.text: Departments and budget staff would have had less than four weeks to prepare and add every omitted request.
unfair_wording.why: No source raised this burden, and the line overstates it. The resolution gave departments an 'opportunity' to submit omitted requests, not a duty (P-031), and the officials said they had already sent their 2027 requests in writing (P-080). Suggested wording: 'Budget staff would have had 25 days to add any omitted requests that departments chose to submit.'

imbalance.issue: Summaries of the commission's role lean on the sponsors' language. The page says it 'is helping draft' (line 8), 'helps draft' (line 50) and helps 'prepare' (line 147), and the Aug 5 entry says it was brought back 'as one did until 2018' (line 16). Yet the operative code makes it the body that submits the proposal (P-005). It also seats two district commissioners, where the 1953-2018 commission's only Board member was the at-large chairman (P-002, P-008). All of these facts are elsewhere on the page (lines 25, 60, 137); the summaries should match them.

Layer 4's source count understates the critics. Line 119 says 'two justice officials and one commissioner criticizing it', but FOX 5 attributes the objection to the six-official 'Justice Leaders' coalition (P-076), and Judge Johnson spoke 'on behalf of the coalition' (P-078). Say 'six justice officials, through two quoted speakers'. The note that the count 'reflects whom the sources quoted' helps but does not fix this.

Quote selection is uneven. The supporters' quoted phrases are substantive ('earlier and ongoing input', 'balanced representation', 'the full Board's exclusive authority'). Two critic quotes isolate single hedge words ('clarify' at line 84, 'effectively' at line 157), and one cuts the strongest words of a cited authority (Pew, line 158). Each is small, but together they make the critics' case read as more tentative than its sources.

label_disagreements.argument: Card 2: Two commissioners, seated under rules they sponsored, have too much say
label_disagreements.label: Who serves in 2027, and how chosen: Supported (county records). Hearings held by the commission: Supported (county notice). How much the two shape the draft: Uncertain (no draft yet). Fairness: a values question
label_disagreements.proposed: Add 'Their role under the code: Supported (the code's text)'. The two 'participate directly and continuously' in reviewing requests, budget assumptions and elected officials' requests, and in preparing the recommended budget that the commission submits (P-013, P-005, P-015). Keep 'How much the two shape the draft: Uncertain'.
label_disagreements.why: The page's own rule says a rule's text settles what the rule says. Card 1 gets 'Rules: Supported (the code's text)' for the sponsors' claims based on the code. Card 2's code-based support (line 147) has no matching label, so the critic card looks less grounded than the record makes it.

label_disagreements.argument: Card 3: The 5% limit keeps departments' full requests out of the draft (conflict with the code)
label_disagreements.label: Conflict with the code: Uncertain (the code mentions no cap)
label_disagreements.proposed: Conflict with the code: Uncertain (the code requires the draft to include the requests of all departments, agencies, elected officials and authorities, but neither allows nor forbids a cap; no legal opinion in our sources)
label_disagreements.why: Uncertain is the right label. But the reason names only the code's silence, which is the point that helps the limit. The 'shall include ... all' requirement the critics rely on belongs beside it, as line 82 already does ('either to allow one or to forbid one').

label_disagreements.argument: Card 3: across-the-board caps are weak budgeting (GFOA and Pew)
label_disagreements.label: Sound budgeting: a values question
label_disagreements.proposed: What GFOA and Pew advise: Uncertain (quoted only in Resolution 26-0729; their own texts not checked; if checked and matching, Supported). Whether a cap is sound budgeting: a values question.
label_disagreements.why: The page's own rule gives each part of a card its own label. Saying that professional bodies criticize across-the-board caps is a factual claim about what those bodies said, not a value judgment. Folding it into 'values' makes the critics' expert backing look like opinion.

label_disagreements.argument: Card 4: The new process is open (openness of meetings)
label_disagreements.label: Hearings announced, slides posted: Supported (county records)
label_disagreements.proposed: October hearings publicly announced: Supported (county notice). Some offices' 2027 slides posted: Supported (data catalog). Other commission meetings open to commissioners and the public: Uncertain (no notice found; staff set the schedule, P-015).
label_disagreements.why: Ellis said the commission's meetings are open and that all commissioners can attend. The records settle only that the October hearings were announced and that some offices' slides were posted. The card's own 'What's uncertain' says the openness of other meetings is unknown. The label should say that too, instead of a blanket 'Supported' covering facts the page added.

label_disagreements.argument: Card 4: more transparent than recent years
label_disagreements.label: More open than past years: Uncertain (his statement; 2026 also had hearings)
label_disagreements.proposed: More open than past years: Uncertain (his statement; the 2026 cycle also had formal hearings and printed all extra requests in an appendix, P-049)
label_disagreements.why: The appendix is a county record, the critics' main point on transparency, and already appears in the card's challenges. The label's reason should not mention only the hearings.

questions_to_weigh: They are neutral, and I would accept them as fair. Q1 offers the whole Board as an option and asks how commissioner members should be chosen, which is Barrett's issue. Q2 describes the limit in the critics' own terms ('only in narrative form'), and Q3 and Q4 are even-handed. One gap: the justice officials' main objection was about who hears their requests, a two-commissioner panel or the full Board (P-076). Q1 covers that only indirectly, as 'who should shape the first draft.' Suggested addition: 'Should departments and elected officials present their budget requests to the commission or to the full Board?'
verdict_summary: Fair overall, and close to full strength. Critics get four of the six cards and verbatim quotes, including 'hijack' and 'shenanigans'. They also get: a Supported label showing that the 2027 rules seated their own sponsors without a vote; the code's 'shall include ... all' requirement; the 2026 appendix; the public defender's request at 3.3 times the cap; the 0.4% evidence that whoever drafts largely sets the budget; and an explicit note that no source gives any reason for the 5% limit or for filing the resolution to remove it. The remaining tilt is modest. The page repeatedly says the commission 'helps' draft (the sponsors' 'assist' framing), though it now submits the proposal. Card 3's 'Requests above 5% can still be seen' generalizes from one office's slides, which are not the draft. Two critic phrases are quoted as single hedge words. And some record-based support for the critics is shortened or misplaced: P-013's full role for the two commissioners, the 2026 increases for four of the six protesting offices together with P-028's 'true picture' reason, the scale of unmet requests in P-051, and the sheriff's staffing slides. Labels are mostly fair. Card 2 lacks a code-text 'Supported' label to match card 1's, and card 4's 'Supported' covers the October notice rather than Ellis's broader claim. No label is more generous to the critics than the evidence.
